take_homes: Find out what job the teammate is actually trying to get done before I decide what to share. Pick the sharing shape on whether it moves their outcome, not on what's convenient for us.
My plan is not finished while the people plan is full of unnamed roles. Someone has to own, govern and answer for it, and that doesn't travel with the files.
Test the switch, not the solution: ask what would have to be true for this person to drop their current way of working. One conversation with them comes first.

monday.move: Message one person from the pricing working group and ask for twenty minutes on how they build the usage numbers today. I'll show nothing and pitch nothing.
monday.who: The one on the pricing working group who builds the usage numbers that go to the CFO. I'll pick the person myself.
monday.when: Send the message first thing Monday and have the conversation within the week.
monday.stop_condition: If their answer shows they'd rather get a pushed brief than build their own agent, I stop planning to share the folder and design the push version instead.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files. Everyone keeps their own copy, so even the folder option has nowhere to live yet.

misconception.why: Nothing in the hour was about prompt wording. What decided the outcome was the teammate's job, who absorbs the thing, and who is accountable. I still think good prompts matter inside a skill, so it's shaken rather than changed.

one_line: Useful, because it made me talk to the person before building anything for them. But it says 'access isn't absorption' about four times.
